title: The Smoke Still Finds Me
logline: A woman far from home remembers how her grandmother taught her the coffee ceremony, and learns that it was never about the coffee.

audience.who: TODO(you): e.g. young Ethiopians aged 18-30 living away from their family's home town or abroad
audience.where: TODO(you): e.g. on a phone, vertical, TikTok / Instagram / YouTube Shorts, sound on
audience.feel: TODO(you): e.g. the urge to call a grandparent today

characters.name: Etenesh (grandmother)
characters.description: Etenesh, a 74-year-old Ethiopian Amhara grandmother from the northern highlands: slender, warm medium-dark brown skin with fine wrinkles, long oval Habesha face, high cheekbones, slim straight nose, large dark almond-shaped eyes, gentle smile lines, a small faded blue-green cross tattoo in the centre of her forehead; grey hair in fine flat shuruba braids close to the scalp, mostly covered by a white cotton netela shawl draped over her head and shoulders with a narrow green-yellow-red tibeb border; long white cotton habesha kemis dress with tibeb embroidery down the front; a small silver Ethiopian Orthodox cross on a black cord
characters.short: Etenesh: 74-year-old Ethiopian Amhara grandmother, warm medium-dark brown skin, long oval face, high cheekbones, slim nose, small faded cross tattoo on the forehead, grey shuruba braids under a white netela draped over her head and shoulders, white habesha kemis with green-yellow-red tibeb border

characters.name: Liya (granddaughter, age 10)
characters.description: Liya, Etenesh's 10-year-old granddaughter, an Ethiopian Habesha girl: slim, warm brown skin, oval face, high cheekbones, slim nose, big bright dark almond-shaped eyes; black hair in neat shuruba cornrow braids running from the forehead to the back of the head, gathered in a small bun; mustard-yellow knitted cardigan over a simple white cotton habesha dress with a narrow tibeb border
characters.short: Liya: 10-year-old Ethiopian Habesha girl, warm brown skin, oval face, big dark almond-shaped eyes, black shuruba cornrow braids in a small bun, mustard-yellow cardigan over a white habesha dress

voice.name: Kore
voice.style: Speak slowly and warmly, like a woman remembering her grandmother. Calm, unhurried, intimate.

shots.reason: Establishing shot: the audience must know this is a highland village at dawn before we meet anyone.
shots.image_prompt: Extreme wide establishing shot at dawn of a small village in the Ethiopian highlands: round tukul houses with mud walls and conical thatched roofs, a dirt path, tall eucalyptus trees, terraced green hills and distant blue mountains under low morning mist; one thin line of grey wood smoke rising from the roof of the nearest tukul; pale gold light on the horizon. No people. Eye level, 24mm lens, deep focus

motion.video_prompt: slow cinematic pan to the right, mist drifts gently over the hills, the thin line of smoke rises, nothing else moves

narration.en: In my grandmother's village, the day began before the sun.

shots.reason: Medium shot introduces Etenesh doing the ritual, so the first face we see is tied to the coffee.
shots.image_prompt: Medium shot inside a dim traditional tukul at dawn. Etenesh sits on a low carved wooden stool, leaning slightly forward, roasting pale green coffee beans in a long-handled flat black iron pan resting on a small clay charcoal brazier on the floor in front of her; her left hand steadies the pan's long handle and her right hand stirs the beans with a short metal rod. Freshly cut green grass and a few yellow meskel daisies are scattered on the earthen floor; a black clay jebena coffee pot stands on a woven straw ring beside the brazier; a small clay incense burner sends up a thin thread of frankincense smoke. Orange ember light on her face, soft daylight from the doorway behind her. Eye level, 35mm lens

narration.en: Every morning, Etenesh roasted coffee over charcoal, the way her mother taught her.

shots.reason: Close-up on the beans gives the sound and smell a picture; it is the detail people remember.
shots.image_prompt: Extreme close-up from a high three-quarter angle of coffee beans roasting in a flat black iron pan over glowing charcoal: the beans are turning from pale green to glossy dark brown, a few cracked open, thin curls of white smoke rising; a short metal stirring rod lies across the rim of the pan. Ember glow from below, dark warm background, macro lens, shallow depth of field. No people

motion.video_prompt: the beans shift slightly, curls of smoke rise slowly, embers pulse softly, static macro camera

narration.en: She said you could hear when the beans were ready. They crackle, like they are laughing.

shots.reason: Introduces Liya and the first contact between the two: the smoke is passed to her.
shots.image_prompt: Medium shot inside the warm tukul. Grandmother Etenesh stands and holds the flat iron pan of freshly roasted dark coffee beans by its long handle with both hands, at chest height, bringing it close to her granddaughter Liya, who sits on a low stool; Liya waves one open hand above the pan to bring the rising fragrant vapour toward her face, eyes open and bright, smiling up at her grandmother. Thin grey wisps rise from the hot beans. Green grass on the floor, warm firelight, soft daylight from the doorway. Both upper bodies fully visible, eye level, 35mm lens

narration.en: She carried the smoke around the room, so everyone could greet it.

shots.reason: Close-up on old hands grinding: years of repetition shown, not told.
shots.image_prompt: Close-up of Etenesh's weathered, wrinkled brown hands grinding roasted coffee: a deep carved wooden mortar stands on the earthen floor, her left hand holds its rim steady, her right hand grips a heavy iron pestle upright and presses it down into the dark roasted beans; dark coffee grounds visible inside the mortar; the edge of her white netela with its green-yellow-red tibeb border falls over her wrist. Warm side light from the fire, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field

narration.en: I watched her hands. Hands that had done this ten thousand times.

shots.reason: The high pour from the jebena is the iconic image of the ceremony and the visual peak of the first half.
shots.image_prompt: Medium close-up, side view. Etenesh kneels by a low wooden coffee tray and pours coffee from a black clay jebena: she holds the jebena by its handle in her right hand, raised about a hand's length above the cups, the spout tilted down, and a thin unbroken stream of dark coffee falls straight down into the first cup. Six small white handleless porcelain cups stand upright in two neat rows on the tray directly below the spout; steam rises from the filled cups. Warm firelight, dark background, 50mm lens, focus on the spout, the stream and the cup

motion.video_prompt: the thin stream of coffee falls steadily into the small cup, steam rises, her hand stays still, static camera

narration.en: The first cup is called abol. Strong, like the morning.

shots.reason: Turning point: the grandmother passes the jebena to Liya. The line of dialogue carries the theme.
shots.image_prompt: Close-up at the low wooden coffee tray. Liya kneels beside her grandmother and holds the black clay jebena by its handle with both small hands, tilting it carefully so a thin stream of coffee pours from the spout into one small white handleless cup that stands upright on the tray; Etenesh's old hand rests lightly under the jebena's round base, helping her hold the angle. Both faces visible above the hands: Etenesh watching with a proud smile, Liya concentrating. Warm firelight, 50mm lens, focus on the hands, the spout and the cup

narration.en: One day she put the jebena in my hands. Slowly, she said. Coffee is not about the coffee.

shots.reason: Wide shot answers her line: the neighbours who come. The film's meaning is the people.
shots.image_prompt: Wide shot inside the tukul, morning light through the open door. Etenesh and three neighbours (an old man wrapped in a white gabi shawl, a middle-aged woman in a white netela, a young man in a plain shirt) sit on low stools in a half circle around the low wooden coffee tray, where the black jebena stands on its straw ring; each adult holds one small white handleless cup upright at chest height with the fingertips. Liya stands and carries one small cup with both hands to the old man, serving the eldest first. A woven basket of popcorn and a bowl of roasted barley on the floor, green grass on the floor; everyone talking and laughing. Eye level, 28mm lens, all faces visible

narration.en: It is about who comes to sit with you.

shots.reason: The empty stool tells us she is gone without saying it; the narrator now keeps the ritual alive.
shots.image_prompt: Medium shot of a small modern apartment kitchen far from Ethiopia at dawn: cool blue light through a window with a view of city rooftops, against the warm glow of a small electric stove where a flat iron pan of coffee beans is roasting, a thin wisp of grey smoke rising toward the window. Beside the stove stands an empty low carved wooden stool; folded on its seat lies a white netela shawl with a green-yellow-red tibeb border; a black clay jebena stands on a straw ring on the counter. No people. Eye level, 35mm lens

narration.en: Now I roast coffee far from home. And every morning, the smoke still finds me. So does she.
